title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Booking Cargo Type in Demurrage Goodwill
content:
The cargo type recorded on the booking shapes demurrage goodwill on a Demurrage and Detention Free Time record in two places: the repricing of the demurrage line, and the part of the goodwill base that goodwill may touch.

## In the repricing

- **Rate class.** Classes follow the equipment class map, except for reefer-mapped units, which stay reefer only when the booking carries reefer cargo and are otherwise repriced as dry.
- **Uplift.** On a dangerous-goods booking the repricing adds to each demurrage day rate the product's uplift percentage of that rate; on any other booking it adds nothing.

## In the goodwill base

Any dangerous-goods uplift inside the gross goodwill base, the figure goodwill starts from, is money the line hands on to the terminal, and goodwill never cuts into it.

- **Dangerous-goods booking:** the portion of the gross goodwill base that is uplift is taken out of it. That share is the fraction of the gross goodwill base obtained by dividing the uplift percentage by 100 increased by the uplift percentage.
- **Any other booking:** nothing is removed.

## Truth table

| Mapped class | Booking cargo type | Class in repricing | Uplift in repricing | Share removed from the gross goodwill base |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| reefer | reefer | reefer | none | none |
| reefer | dangerous goods | dry | yes | yes |
| reefer | any other | dry | none | none |
| dry or special | dangerous goods | as mapped | yes | yes |
| dry or special | any other | as mapped | none | none |

## Illustration (hypothetical percentage)

With an assumed uplift of 20 percent and a gross goodwill base of 1200.00 on a dangerous-goods booking, the share removed is 20 parts in 120 of 1200.00, which is 200.00, leaving 1000.00 on which goodwill can act.
